proposed.explanation: ABUK (Abu Qir Fertilizers) fits the investor's stated goal of adding a fertilizer exporter for diversification. The verified EPS data shows strong momentum: 9M-2026 EPS of 8.74 EGP versus 4.28 EGP in 9M-2025, a 104% year-on-year increase. Annualising the 9-month EPS (×12/9) gives roughly 11.65 EGP, implying a P/E of about 6.5 at the 76.21 EGP share price – well below typical market multiples, suggesting the stock is not expensive on earnings. The 5-year horizon is compatible with a cyclical commodity/fertiliser name, and the investor keeps a separate emergency fund, so locking in 22,863 EGP (≈35% of the 65,600 EGP portfolio) does not impair liquidity. I chose 300 shares rather than the 430-share maximum allowed by the 50% concentration rule because (a) the absolute revenue and net-profit figures are AMBIGUOUS (see below), so I cannot confirm the scale of earnings or the quality of the 104% jump; (b) the investor's risk tolerance is medium; and (c) the EPS path is volatile (6.62 → 1.23 → 1.99 → 4.28 → 8.74 over five 9-month periods), so a moderate initial position is prudent. After the purchase the portfolio is: Cash 17,137 EGP, COMI 25,600 EGP (39%), ABUK 22,863 EGP (35%) – both holdings stay under the 50% cap. Risks: I could not verify total revenue or net profit because the page's unit line conflicts with the column headers (AMBIGUOUS), so the absolute size of the profit base is unconfirmed. There is no balance-sheet, dividend, or export-revenue-breakdown data in the evidence. Fertiliser prices are commodity-linked and can swing sharply. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
